challenges: Contact follow-up is 32023/36218 (88.4%) on page 5, below the 95% threshold; page 11 instead prints 31923/36218 (88.1%). Among 549 validated suspects, 449 were investigated and 236 transferred. One hundred remain uninvestigated (85 Nord-Kivu, 12 Ituri, three Tshopo); none of 24 Bas-Uele suspects was transferred.

Butuhe and Avakubi remain closed for security reasons. Sud-Kivu reporting is 5/9 and three PoEs lack isolation facilities. Bas-Uele has four of 20 points not reporting and 88% traveler sensitisation. At Pluto, 969/3247 travelers refused screening. The Nord-Kivu referral to CSR Kyavinyonge rather than CT/CTE conflicts with the printed 100% transfer rate.

Tshopo: seven of 107 facilities exceed 80% PCI score, 17/20 lack water and 130/632 providers are trained. One body was not swabbed and household resistance persists. Haut-Uele reports five confirmed cases in the community preventing household decontamination, and PCI supervision not activated in four zones. Nord-Kivu household decontamination is 11/33.

Tshopo reports four confirmed cases refusing hospitalisation and an infected CTE nurse. Bas-Uele isolation patients lack nutritional support and one escaped; CTE construction continues. Haut-Uele reports one confirmed patient escaping, Pawa ambulance maintenance and network gaps. Ituri lacks blood; 11 Mandima patients received no food, Biakato May lacks drinking water and Biakato Mines decontaminates bodies in the room with living patients. Nord-Kivu has 107/447 patients outside CTE/CT and uses eight of 14 ambulances.

Ituri reports 1613 people vaccinated, 31 MAPI including five serious events, and the TUMAINI trial launched. Bas-Uele reports 1660/13202 vaccinated, non-operating cold-chain units and insufficient vaccines and funds. Haut-Uele frontline vaccination is halted after Isiro generator failure. Nord-Kivu and Tshopo vaccination data did not arrive. Ervebo efficacy against BDBV remains under research; these observations establish no efficacy.

Katwa lacks adequate triage, simplified continuity and absenteeism plans, PPE, blood products and an ambulance; 18/178 staff are absent and three quarantined. Ituri survivor follow-up is 472/717, with clinic overuse and stockouts. Tshopo has unfinished continuity work, non-operating incinerators and declining maternal/child service use. Haut-Uele reports free-care subsidy gaps in seven affected zones, delayed catch-up vaccination and interrupted chronic care at Wamba.

Ituri community reporting covers 12/28 zones and seven of nine incidents were resolved. Nord-Kivu received 445/650 expected community alerts, resolved one of eight incidents and engaged 2186/4750 people. Haut-Uele identified and transferred five hidden patients. Tshopo reports response-team attack and arson; the security section lists Bafwasende under Nord-Kivu, an attribution conflict retained rather than repaired.

Ituri psychosocial pillar daily case denominator 27 and Nord-Kivu 28 differ from headline 28/29; preserve pillar scope. Haut-Uele lacks creches, nutritional kits and mobility; Wamba data did not arrive. Nord-Kivu reports weak support in nine zones and no creches in ten affected zones. Bas-Uele confirmed-case support is delayed; Tshopo has training, communications and transport gaps.

Tshopo reports 115 motorcycles still missing while CTE construction and laboratory maintenance continue. Bas-Uele received 200 litres of diesel but lacks ambulances, computers and team mobility. Response-team attack and Bafwasende arson are reported; Avakubi and Butuhe remain closed. Preserve the province attribution conflict between CREC and security sections.

National PSEA figures cover 16-22 October: 12/56 zones undertook activities and four of 15 partners supported them. Other current provincial observations report missing collection tools and complaint mechanisms in Tshopo, low mechanism awareness in Ituri, Nord-Kivu and Haut-Uele, no Haut-Uele partner reports and missing Bas-Uele data. The national weekly figures are not redated to 23 October.
